faq.title: Questions that come up in every first conversation
faq.subtitle: Five answers so our 30-minute call can focus on your situation.

q1.question: How is Clyde different from ChatGPT or Jasper?
q1.answer: ChatGPT and Jasper are generic tools without memory. You have to supply context with every prompt. Clyde has a separate memory for each client: brand voice, audience, goals and working agreements are kept. On top of that, Clyde orchestrates ten live skills plus two coming soon (social, blogs, ads, email, lead qualification, SEO, analytics and more), not just text. One brain with shared memory, not a separate tool per task.

q2.question: What if I want to cancel?
q2.answer: You're not locked in. What Clyde knows about your clients is yours. After cancellation you have 30 days to take your data with you; after that we delete your workspaces. Your data sits on servers and in a database in the EU.

q3.question: Why an application? Why no self-service?
q3.answer: Clyde is a high-touch AI partnership, not a SaaS tool. Every client gets personal onboarding by Daley (founder) and 4 weeks of partnership setup. We accept a maximum of {maxPartners} new agencies per year. The application is not there to reject you: we check together whether it is a match for both sides. A generic sign-up doesn't fit what we deliver.

q4.question: Exactly how many skills do I get?
q4.answer: Twelve in total: 10 live (Social Media, Blog Factory, Ad Manager, Lead Qualifier, Email Management, ManyChat DM, Reporting, SEO/GEO, Research, Clyde orchestrator) and 2 coming soon (Voice Agent, Reel Builder). Every plan uses all live skills; caps apply to the heavier ones, except on Enterprise.

q5.question: Why does this work better for agencies than separate tools?
q5.answer: Because it is one brain with shared memory, not 12 separate tools. What Clyde learns about a client in social media, he also uses in that client's blogs and ads. With separate tools you lose that context at every handover. One colleague for your whole portfolio means that what he knows about a client travels between skills.

q1.question: Why caps per skill instead of "everything unlimited"?
q1.answer: Voice, Video Ads and Reel Builder are the most expensive skills in credit usage (5 to 25 credits per action). Unlimited on every tier would lead to astronomical prices, or to fair-use throttling behind the scenes. Caps keep costs predictable and give each tier a natural upgrade trigger.

q2.question: What happens if I go over my credits or caps?
q2.answer: When your credits run out, Clyde stops taking actions that cost credits. You then choose: wait until next month, buy a credit pack (Mini Top-Up €39 to Max €697), or upgrade to a higher tier. No automatic overage, no surprise on your invoice.

q3.question: Can I upgrade or downgrade between tiers?
q3.answer: Upgrading is possible at any time. Downgrading takes effect at the next billing cycle. You cannot drop below Founding: your Founding price stays valid for life as long as you remain active.

q4.question: Do I get all skills or a subset?
q4.answer: Every tier gets all skills: 10 live today, Voice Agent and Reel Builder to follow. Caps per tier apply to the heavier ones. Founding's caps sit between Growth and Professional, for €997 for life. Enterprise has no caps (fair use).

q5.question: What is included in the onboarding fee?
q5.answer: The one-time onboarding fee covers 4 weeks of partnership setup by Daley: brand voice intake per brand, KPI definitions, skill configuration, test runs and approval workflow setup. It is not a technical installation fee: it is an investment in a colleague who actually runs with your team.

q6.question: Can I cancel or pause mid-term?
q6.answer: Every tier has monthly cancellation rights: you end at the next billing cycle, without a fee. Pausing is possible by arrangement, with your tier price preserved. Founding members cannot pause without losing their lifetime price: that is the nature of the Founding contract.

q7.question: What exactly happens when I downgrade?
q7.answer: Downgrading takes effect at the next billing cycle. Your clients, their memory and your settings stay in place; from then on the caps of the lower tier apply. You cannot downgrade from Founding: doing so permanently forfeits the lifetime price.

q8.question: Who owns the data and can I export it?
q8.answer: All data, brand voice profiles, content and reports, stays yours. After cancellation you have 30 days to take your data with you; after that we delete it. No lock-in, no renegotiation, no hidden exit fees.

service_description.title: 1. Service description

meta.title: Privacy policy | Future Marketing AI
meta.description: Privacy policy of Future Marketing AI. How we collect, use, and protect personal data under GDPR. Sub-processors, retention periods, your rights.

privacy.content: This privacy policy describes how Future Marketing AI (FutureMarketingAI) collects, uses, stores and protects personal data in connection with our platform around Clyde, the AI colleague for agencies. FutureMarketingAI is committed to protecting the privacy of our subscribers, their clients and end users, in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable Dutch data protection laws. This policy applies to all data processed through our platform and website.

data_collected.title: 1. Data we collect
data_collected.content: We collect the following categories of personal data: Account data (name, email address, company name, billing information), Client workspace data (brand voice documents, social media account connections, content schedules, audience profiles), Usage data (platform activity logs, feature usage, execution counts) and AI interaction data (chat messages with AI agents, voice call transcripts, content generation prompts). We do not intentionally collect special categories of personal data (special categories under GDPR Article 9).

purpose_of_processing.title: 2. Purpose of processing
purpose_of_processing.content: We process personal data for the following purposes: providing the services of Clyde, the AI colleague for agencies (content creation, voice agent operations, lead qualification, social media management, ad creation, reporting), improving service quality and AI performance through aggregated usage analysis, billing and subscription management, providing technical support and customer service, and complying with legal obligations including tax, accounting and regulatory requirements.

legal_basis.title: 3. Legal basis
legal_basis.content: Our processing of personal data is based on the following legal grounds: performance of a contract (GDPR Article 6(1)(b)) for providing our subscribed services, legitimate interest (GDPR Article 6(1)(f)) for service improvement, security monitoring and fraud prevention, consent (GDPR Article 6(1)(a)) for analytics cookies and optional marketing communications, and legal obligation (GDPR Article 6(1)(c)) for tax and regulatory compliance.

ai_data_processing.title: 4. AI data processing
ai_data_processing.content: Clyde, our AI colleague, processes data as follows: the Content Creator skill uses brand voice documents and content briefs to generate marketing content. Only the minimum context needed is sent to AI providers. The Voice Agent skill processes call audio for speech recognition and response generation. Recordings are retained for 90 days for quality assurance. The Lead Qualifier skill analyzes form submissions and chat messages to score and route leads. Lead scoring is advisory; no automated decisions are made. AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic) process data under a Zero Data Retention policy, meaning your data is not used to train AI models.

sub_processors.title: 5. Sub-processors
sub_processors.content: We use the following key sub-processors to deliver our services: OpenAI (content generation, US with EU Data Privacy Framework certification), Anthropic (content generation, US with EU Data Privacy Framework certification), Supabase (database and authentication, EU region, Frankfurt), Vercel (hosting and CDN, EU and global regions) and Vapi (voice agent processing, US). A complete and current list of sub-processors is maintained in our Data Processing Agreement. We notify subscribers at least 30 days in advance of new sub-processors.

data_retention.title: 6. Data retention
data_retention.content: Active accounts: all data is retained for the duration of the service agreement. After termination: a 30-day export window is provided, after which all data is permanently deleted. Voice recordings and chat logs: retained for 90 days after processing for quality assurance and dispute resolution. Platform logs: retained for 90 days. Backups: deleted within 30 days after deletion of source data. Billing records: retained in accordance with Dutch tax law (7 years).

data_subject_rights.title: 7. Your rights
data_subject_rights.content: Under the GDPR, you have the right to: access your personal data and receive a copy, rectify inaccurate or incomplete personal data, erase your personal data (right to be forgotten), restrict the processing of your personal data, data portability (receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format), object to processing based on legitimate interest and withdraw consent at any time for consent-based processing. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@future-marketing.ai. We respond within 30 days as required by the GDPR.

international_transfers.title: 8. International data transfers
international_transfers.content: Some of our sub-processors are located outside the EU/EEA, mainly in the United States. For these transfers we rely on the following safeguards: the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) for certified US companies (OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel, Stripe) and Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) approved by the European Commission where DPF certification is not available. Where possible we use EU data center regions to minimize international transfers. We closely follow legal developments around international transfers, including any challenges to the DPF.

ai_readiness_assessment.title: 9. AI Readiness Assessment
ai_readiness_assessment.content: Our AI Readiness Scan at /assessment is an interactive questionnaire that produces a persona, scores and a recommended roadmap. What we collect: email address (upon confirmed sign-up), your answers to the sixteen questions, calculated scores and persona assignment, a hashed IP and user agent for rate limiting and abuse prevention, and a timestamp of your consent. Purpose: to deliver the report to you, improve the scan product and (only with explicit opt-in) send a newsletter about AI marketing. Legal basis: your consent (GDPR art. 6(1)(a)), captured via double opt-in. Retention: answers, scores and consent records are kept for 12 months and then automatically deleted. Processors: Supabase (EU region) for storage, Resend for email delivery, Vercel for hosting. Your rights: you can withdraw, request access or deletion at any time via privacy@future-marketing.ai. We respond within 30 days.

platform_data.title: 10. Instagram and Facebook data (Meta platform data)
platform_data.content:
When a client connects an Instagram or Facebook business account, we receive the following through Meta's official APIs: the platform account id and username, public profile information, the content scheduled and published through our platform, and metrics about that content (reach, interactions, follower counts). If the client enables the inbox feature, we also receive messages and comments addressed to the connected account.

Purpose: scheduling, publishing and reporting on content on behalf of the client, and replying to messages within the connected account. We use this data for nothing else. We do not sell it, do not share it with advertisers, and do not use it for ad targeting or profiling outside the connected account.

Legal basis: performance of the contract with the agency (GDPR art. 6(1)(b)); for messages and comments, additionally the consent of the account holder who authorises the connection.

Retention: platform data is kept for as long as the connection is active. As soon as the connection is removed, or the app is removed from the Instagram or Facebook account, we immediately delete that account's platform identifiers and stored access tokens. Content and reports already produced remain part of the agency's own records and are erased on request.

Deletion: remove the app through your Instagram or Facebook settings. We then receive a deletion request automatically and show you a confirmation code. Instructions and the status of a request are at https://app.future-marketing.ai/data-deletion. You can also request deletion directly at privacy@future-marketing.ai.

We process this data in accordance with the Meta Platform Terms and the Meta Developer Policies.

contact.title: 11. Contact and supervisory authority

If you believe your data protection rights have been violated, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, AP) at autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl.

warm.clydeAnswer: Less text per slide, and ending with a question instead of a link. She asked for that two weeks ago when she rejected a draft; I have applied it ever since.

cold.description: The goals from the strategy session, the pillars and the research into the market, competitors and audience. Clyde checks his proposals against them.

cold.clydeAnswer: Yes, under the skin knowledge pillar. The goal this quarter is reach among new followers, so I will turn it into a carousel people want to share.

context.name: Who the brand is
context.description: The core that always travels along: the client profile, the brand voice, the audience and what is and is not allowed. Clyde keeps it up to date: your corrections go into it, and every night he updates the summary.
context.prompt: Write a caption for the new night cream.
context.clydeAnswer: Tone: warm, direct, no capitalized You. Audience: women 28-44 who value rituals. No claims, results expressed in concrete weeks. Caption opens with the evening routine, ends with a question instead of a CTA.

isolation.title: Separated per client
isolation.body1: Clyde works for several agencies and their clients at the same time. Each client has its own workspace with its own memory: when Clyde works for client A, he retrieves client A's memory, not client B's. That way a brand voice does not jump over to another client.
isolation.body2: Technically, every memory about a client is tied to that agency and that client in the database, and every lookup filters on them. After cancellation you have 30 days to take your data with you; after that we delete it.

decay.title: Sharper every day, never cluttered
decay.decayBody: Not everything from the past stays equally relevant. Old details slowly lose weight, so Clyde does not get clogged up with data from six months ago. Important patterns stay, noise recedes. Just like with humans.
decay.dreamBody: At night Clyde does what we do in our sleep: he connects the dots, abstracts patterns and writes important insights into his permanent knowledge. You wake up with a colleague who is smarter than yesterday.

q1.text: Have you written down an AI strategy for your agency?

options.a: No, we experiment ad hoc per employee
options.b: Verbal plans, nothing on paper yet
options.c: A written 6 to 12 month plan with owners
options.d: AI is part of our agency strategy with measurable KPIs

q2.text: How involved is leadership in AI decisions?

options.a: Leadership doesn't quite know what we do with AI
options.d: Leadership actively steers and positions this publicly

q3.text: How do you measure the impact of AI on your own agency margins?

options.b: We feel a margin lift but do not count it
options.c: Per project or client we calculate AI time saved
options.d: AI contribution sits in our pricing strategy and margin reports

q4.text: We have established which AI tools are safe for client data and our IP liability.

q5.text: How well organised is your client and brand data (assets, brand voice, KPIs)?

options.a: Scattered across Drive, Notion and people's heads
options.b: One folder per client, inconsistently filled
options.c: Centralised in DAM or CMS, but AI tools can't access it directly
options.d: Per brand, a knowledge base that AI tools read directly

q6.text: How do you measure content and campaign performance per client?

options.b: Central dashboard with basic metrics, manual updates
options.d: Real-time cross-channel attribution with anomaly alerts

q7.text: Our clients receive reports where AI-driven and human-driven outcomes are clearly distinguishable.

q8.text: Which 1st-party data do you structurally feed into AI as input?

options.a: None, we run on generic content inspiration
options.b: Client briefings, sometimes a brand doc
options.c: Brand voice plus persona docs structurally as input
options.d: Client data, brand and performance data flow continuously into pipelines

q9.text: Which AI tools run systematically in your workflow?

options.a: Mostly ChatGPT, individual use per employee
options.b: ChatGPT plus 1 or 2 fixed tools, shared team-wide
options.d: AI orchestrator drives multiple tools per workflow autonomously

q10.text: How deep is automation in your content operation?

options.a: Manual, with AI help on isolated tasks
options.b: A few Zapier or Make flows running
options.c: Pipelines from brief to publish largely automated
options.d: End-to-end content factory runs autonomously per brand

q11.text: How dependent are you on a single AI vendor?

options.a: Fully, if that vendor is down we're stuck
options.c: Multi-vendor through a gateway, switching is days
options.d: Vendor-agnostic stack, EU hosting, our own data

q12.text: How fast can you get a new AI tool live in production?

options.a: Months, if it ships at all
options.d: Directly via API in our existing stack

q13.text: How many employees use AI at least weekly for work?

options.b: About a quarter of the team
options.d: Everyone, AI is a standard part of the workflow

q14.text: Who decides which client data is allowed into AI tools?

options.a: No one explicitly; employees decide on their own
options.b: The project lead decides case by case
options.c: One person (founder or lead) approves upfront
options.d: Documented approval flow with audit trail per client

q15.text: Our clients know which parts of their campaign are AI-driven.

q16.text: How often do you train the team on new AI skills?

options.a: Never; people learn on their own
options.b: Ad hoc, when something new appears
options.d: Structured curriculum plus AI literacy for the whole team

tooling-led.name: Workflow Agency
tooling-led.identity: the builder with too many disconnected tools and too little central brain

team-led.name: People Agency

team-led.week1: Identify one task that costs your best team member at least two hours every week. That's your first automation target.

balanced.identity: the agency without a weak link,but also without a sharp distinguishing profile
